newsitem.title: USA: Federal Reserve rate changes since Sept. 1992.
newsitem.headline: Federal Reserve rate changes since Sept. 1992.

text.p: Following is a list of the Federal Reserve's interest rate moves since it cut the federal funds rate on Sept. 4, 1992.
- Sept. 4, 1992 - Fed funds rate cut to 3.0 percent.
- Feb. 4, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 3.25 percent.
- March 23, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 3.5 percent.
- April 18, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 3.75 percent.
- May 17, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 4.25 percent, discount rate raised to 3.5 percent.
- Aug. 16, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 4.75 percent, discount rate raised to 4.0 percent.
- Nov. 15, 1994 - Fed funds rate raised to 5.5 percent, discount rate raised to 4.75 percent.
- Feb. 1, 1995 - Fed funds rate raised to 6.0 percent, discount rate raised to 5.25 percent.
- July 6, 1995 - Fed funds rate lowered to 5.75 percent.
- Dec. 19, 1995 - Fed funds rate lowered to 5.5 percent.
- Jan. 31, 1996 - Fed funds rate lowered to 5.25 percent, discount rate lowered to 5.0 percent.
- March 25, 1997 - Fed funds rate raised to 5.5 percent.
- May 20, 1997 - Fed funds rate left unchanged.
The federal funds rate is the interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The discount rate is the rate the Fed charges banks for loans.
